To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) software modeling is more used for safety-critical systems than for non-critical ones; (2) practitioners with a higher degree of software modeling experience tend to use software modeling more; (3) software modeling is less used in the automotive and medical industries than in the aerospace, defense and telecommunications industries; (4) software modeling is also more used in the aerospace, automotive, and medical industries than the telecommunications industry.

the degree of software modeling usage is significantly correlated with practitioner demographics, e. g., the degree of software model usage is significantly correlated to the target sector of the embedded software products, and to the years of experience in the embedded software development.

(1) the degree of software modeling is higher in sectors of consumer electronics, medical, and automotive than in the sectors of industrial, military and aerospace; (2) the degree of using software model is higher in the sectors of embedded systems, software engineering and systems engineering than in the sectors related to computer science, information systems and business.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
practitioners with higher education level, more experience, and in larger companies are more likely to use software modeling.
the usage of software modeling is not correlated with the demographics of the practitioners.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

software modeling practices are not significantly correlated with practitioner demographics, but the usage of software modeling in the industry is significantly different in terms of the target sectors of the embedded systems.
software modeling is used more in the sectors of automotive and aerospace than in other sectors, and the degree of using software models is higher for practitioners with higher education level.

the degree of using software models is positively associated with the degree of education of the practitioners, and negatively associated with the degree that practitioners work in the embedded software sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there exists a strong positive correlation between the degree of using software models and the target sectors of the embedded systems.
the software modeling practice is significantly different among practitioners with different demographic backgrounds.
the software modeling practices are significantly affected by practitioner demographics, e. g., education level, job position, and company size.
